newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish premier demands discipline in EU dealings.
newsitem.headline: Polish premier demands discipline in EU dealings.

text.p: Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz on Tuesday denounced some EU states for taking unfair advantage of aspiring member Poland's weak negotiating position to enforce their demands over trade issues.
He also warned senior Warsaw officials that if they once again repeated recent failures to fully coordinate Polish policy towards the European Union they would be fired.
Poland, submitting to Spanish demands, on Tuesday cut to seven percent from 22 percent its VAT on imported citrus fruit.

If it had not, this would have derailed Wednesday's crucial annual Association Council meeting of EU and Polish foreign ministers in Luxembourg, a step in Poland's progress towards membership of the Union.

"Poland is waiting within a few months for an opinion from the European Commission about its candidacy and very much will depend on this opinion when it comes to the course of negotiations about our membership," Cimoszewicz told public radio, adding that this weakened Poland's position.
"Unfortunately, some countries of the Union are playing on their advantage from this situation," he said. @

"The Spanish put forward demands concerning tax on imported citrus in a form that is hard to accept," he said, adding that last week he had told EU ambassadors what he thought of the situation "in a very hard and bitter way."
Poland and nine other central and eastern European countries are awaiting the European Commission's advice to EU governments on how suitable they are for EU membership.
Cimoszewicz last year formed a special European Integration Committee, which he heads, to coordinate the actions of various Polish departments in their dealings with the EU. @
But he told reporters before a government meeting that several had failed to respect this arrangement and singled out finance ministry actions over the citrus fruit issue.

"I have said...that if there is one more example of neglecting what the law says about the committee, from whatever official or whatever ministry...then vice ministers responsible for European integration will be sacked," he said.
Spain regarded Poland's 22 percent value-added-tax against citrus fruit as a mechanism designed to protect the country's strawberries and raspberries. @

Poland has said scrapping the tax may cost it $65 million in revenues and it hopes for European Union understanding for its bid to gain better access for its farm products to address the Polish deficit in food trade with the union.

At Wednesday's meeting the EU and Poland will discuss help for Poland's steel industry and are expected to try to end disputes over car assembly regulations as well as an understanding on Poland's fuels sector.
